questions.question:
Choose the correctly spelled comparative form to complete the sentence:
"After three months of physical training, the candidate was much ___ than before."

options.text: fiter
fitter
more fit
more fitter

questions.explanation: Base adjective 'fit' monosyllabic (single syllable) hai aur single short vowel (i) ke baad single consonant (t) par end hota hai (CVC pattern). Aise adjectives mein comparative '-er' lagane se pehle final consonant double ho jata hai: f-i-t-t-e-r. Option D ('more fitter') double comparative error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Regular Inflections & CVC Consonant Doubling.
questions.hint: Check karein ki kya 'fit' short vowel + single consonant par end ho raha hai? Final consonant double hoga ya single?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate word:
"The High Court registrar ordered that no ___ adjournment would be granted in the ongoing criminal appeal."

options.text: farther
further
farthest
furthest

questions.explanation: Yahan context 'additional / extra' (aur aage ki) tareekh ya sthagan ka hai. Physical geographical distance (km/miles) ke liye 'farther' lagta hai, jabki additional time, progression ya extension ke liye strictly 'FURTHER' lagta hai: 'no further adjournment'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Irregular Adjectives & Suppletive Grading — Farther (Distance) vs Further (Additional).
questions.hint: Kya yahan road distance measure ho raha hai ya additional sthagan (adjournment) ki baat ho rahi hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence free from double comparison error:

options.text: The new optical scanner is more faster than the old manual scanner.
The new optical scanner is faster than the old manual scanner.
The new optical scanner is much more faster than the old manual scanner.
The new optical scanner is more fast than the old manual scanner.

questions.explanation: Single-syllable adjective 'fast' ka comparative form '-er' lagakar 'faster' banta hai. 'Faster' ke sath additional 'more' lagana redundant double comparative error (pleonasm) hai. Sahi form sirf 'faster' hai (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Double Comparative & Superlative Ban (Pleonasm).
questions.hint: Check karein ki kya comparative adjective ke aage unnecessary 'more' laga hua hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly completes the affirmative statement:
"In the examination, speed is ___ accuracy for high scoring."

options.text: so important as
as important as
as important than
so important than

questions.explanation: Affirmative sentences mein equality express karne ke liye strictly 'as + adjective + as' construction use hota hai ('as important as'). 'so...as' strictly NEGATIVE sentences mein valid hota hai ('not so important as'). Affirmative mein 'so...as' lagana grammatical error hai, aur 'than' positive degree ke sath aa hi nahi sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Equality ('as...as') vs Inequality ('not as/so...as').
questions.hint: Sentence affirmative hai. Kya affirmative sentence mein 'so...as' valid hota hai ya strictly 'as...as'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The Chief System Officer is five years senior ___ the assistant programmer."

options.text: than
to
from
over

questions.explanation: Latin origin ke adjectives ending in '-or' (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) general English comparative conjunction 'than' nahi lete. Inke comparison ka target hamesha preposition 'TO' se connect hota hai: 'senior TO the assistant programmer'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The Latin Comparative Law: '-OR' Adjectives Take 'TO'.
questions.hint: Adjectives ending in '-or' (senior, junior, prior) ke baad 'than' lagta hai ya 'to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: The judicial registrar prefers electronic documentation than physical paper files.
The judicial registrar prefers electronic documentation to physical paper files.
The judicial registrar more prefers electronic documentation than physical paper files.
The judicial registrar prefers electronic documentation over physical paper files than others.

questions.explanation: Verb 'prefer' aur adjective 'preferable' do options ke comparative link ke liye preposition 'TO' demand karte hain ('prefer X to Y'). Inke sath 'than' lagana standard syntax ka violation hai. Option B bilkul flawless hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: The 'Prefer...To' and 'Preferable To' Law.
questions.hint: 'Prefer' ke sath comparison marker 'than' hota hai ya 'to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Which option corrects the faulty comparison in the sentence?
"The bandwidth of the High Court server is higher than the district court."

options.text: The bandwidth of the High Court server is higher than that of the district court.
The bandwidth of the High Court server is higher than those of the district court.
The bandwidth of the High Court server is higher then the district court.
The bandwidth of the High Court server is more higher than the district court.

questions.explanation: Original sentence mein High Court server ke 'bandwidth' ka comparison seedhe 'district court' se kiya ja raha hai (Bandwidth vs Court = Illogical Comparison). Sahi comparison district court ke bandwidth se hona chahiye. Bandwidth singular uncountable noun hai, isliye singular pronoun 'THAT OF' lagaya jayega: 'higher than that of the district court'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Logical Equivalence in Comparisons: 'That of' & 'Those of'.
questions.hint: Kya 'bandwidth' ka comparison court se ho sakta hai? Bandwidth singular hai toh 'that of' aayega ya 'those of'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly applies the self-exclusion rule in group comparative degree:

options.text: Copper is a better conductor of electricity than any metal.
Copper is a better conductor of electricity than any other metal.
Copper is a better conductor of electricity than any other metals.
Copper is a better conductor of electricity than all other metal.

questions.explanation: Copper khud ek metal hai. Comparative degree mein jab subject usi category ke doosre members se compare ho, toh subject ko exclude karne ke liye 'OTHER' lagana mandatory hai. Formula: 'than any other + singular noun' ('than any other metal'). Option A mein 'other' missing hai, Option C mein 'any other' ke sath plural noun 'metals' galat hai, aur Option D mein 'all other' ke sath singular 'metal' discord hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Group Self-Exclusion: 'Than Any Other + Singular Noun'.
questions.hint: Copper khud ek metal hai. 'Any other' ke baad singular noun lagta hai ya plural?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Find the error part in the following sentence:
"Justice Banerjee is (A) / considered one of the (B) / most impartial judge (C) / on the constitutional bench. (D)"

options.text: Part A (Justice Banerjee is)
Part B (considered one of the)
Part C (most impartial judge)
Part D (on the constitutional bench)

questions.explanation: Part C mein error hai. 'One of the + superlative' construction ke baad aane wala noun hamesha PLURAL hota hai, kyunki chunav (selection) hamesha multiple members mein se hi ho sakta hai. Sahi phrase 'most impartial judges' hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: The 'One of the' Superlative Concord Formula.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ke baad aane wala noun singular hota hai ya plural?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Two Qualities of the Same Entity
questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence comparing two qualities of the same person:

options.text: In handling difficult courtroom situations, the magistrate was braver than wise.
In handling difficult courtroom situations, the magistrate was more brave than wise.
In handling difficult courtroom situations, the magistrate was more braver than wise.
In handling difficult courtroom situations, the magistrate was bravest than wise.

questions.explanation: Jab do alag persons ka comparison nahi ho raha ho, balki EK HI VYAKTI ki DO ALAG QUALITIES (brave vs wise) compare ho rahi hon, toh '-er' suffix use karna prohibited hota hai. Rule demands 'MORE + Positive Adjective 1 + than + Positive Adjective 2'. Isliye 'more brave than wise' strictly correct hai (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: Two Qualities of the Same Entity ('More...Than').
questions.hint: Jab ek hi vyakti ki 2 qualities compare hon, toh '-er' lagta hai ya 'more + base adjective'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct pair of quantifiers:
"The automated cause list generated ___ clerical errors and required ___ manual effort from the staff."

options.text: less, fewer
fewer, less
less, less
fewer, fewer

questions.explanation: 'Clerical errors' plural countable noun hai jisko gina ja sakta hai, isliye iske sath strictly 'FEWER' lagta hai. 'Manual effort' uncountable noun hai (effort ki matra hoti hai), isliye iske sath strictly 'LESS' lagta hai. Isliye correct sequence 'fewer, less' hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Equality & Inequality / Section 5: Quantifier Concord.
questions.hint: 'Errors' countable hain ya uncountable? Aur 'effort' countable hai ya uncountable?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.question:
Transform the following positive sentence into comparative degree without altering its semantic truth:
"The district courtroom is not as spacious as the High Court courtroom."

options.text: The High Court courtroom is not as spacious as the district courtroom.
The district courtroom is more spacious than the High Court courtroom.
The High Court courtroom is more spacious than the district courtroom.
The High Court courtroom is as spacious as the district courtroom.

questions.explanation: Original sentence kehta hai ki district courtroom High Court jitna spacious nahi hai, jiska factual matlab hai ki High Court courtroom district courtroom se zyada spacious hai (High Court > District Court). Superior entity 'High Court courtroom' ko subject banakar affirmative comparative sentence banaya gaya: 'The High Court courtroom is more spacious than the district courtroom.'
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.hint: Agar district courtroom High Court jitna bada nahi hai, toh kaunsa courtroom zyada bada hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14
